title: STEADFAST TO THE END OF THE FEAST

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "On the sixth day offer eight bulls, two rams and fourteen male lambs a year old, all without defect... On the seventh day offer seven bulls, two rams and fourteen male lambs a year old, all without defect. With the bulls, rams and lambs, offer their grain offerings and drink offerings according to the number specified. Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering." - Num 29:29-34 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The offerings continued to the sixth and seventh days of the feast, faithfully brought right through to the end. The people did not tire of worship or abandon it before the festival was complete. They pressed on, bringing their offerings each day until the appointed time was fulfilled. Their devotion held steady from the first day to the last.

There is real virtue in finishing well. It is easy to start something with energy and hard to see it through to the end. But God's people kept worshipping all the way through, not slackening as the days wore on. The seventh day's offerings were brought as faithfully as the first day's.

This challenges us to persevere in our walk with God, not just to begin well but to endure to the end. Many start the journey of faith with enthusiasm but grow weary along the way. God calls us to keep going, to remain faithful through every season, to finish the race set before us.

The apostle Paul, near the end of his life, could say that he had fought the good fight and finished the race (2 Tim 4:7). This is the goal for all who follow Christ: to endure faithfully to the end. And we can, because the One who began a good work in us will carry it to completion (Phil 1:6). Press on in your devotion, steadfast to the very end.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you finish well, or lose heart before the end?
2. What helps you persevere in your walk with God over the long haul?
3. How does God's promise to complete His work in you give you hope?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me not only to begin well but to finish well. Give me a steadfast devotion that endures to the end, trusting that You who began Your good work in me will carry it to completion. Amen.
